title: The Geometry-to-Algebra Chain
content: The file header documents the full geometry-of-numbers proof chain for the class number bound, which is formalized in Mathlib's `CanonicalEmbedding.ConvexBody` module. The five steps are: (1) embed K into $\mathbb{R}^n$ via all Archimedean completions; (2) an ideal $I \subseteq \mathcal{O}_K$ becomes a lattice with covolume $2^{-r_2}\sqrt{|\mathrm{disc}(K)|}\cdot \mathrm{Nm}(I)$; (3) construct the cross-polytope $B(t) = \{\sum|x_i| + 2\sum|z_j| \leq t\}$; (4) apply Minkowski's convex body theorem to find $\alpha \in I$, $\alpha \neq 0$; (5) bound $|\mathrm{Nm}(\alpha)| \leq M(K) \cdot \mathrm{Nm}(I)$, so $\alpha I^{-1}$ is a bounded-norm representative of the inverse class.
mathContext: $M(K) = \left(\frac{4}{\pi}\right)^{r_2} \cdot \frac{n!}{n^n} \cdot \sqrt{|\mathrm{disc}(K)|}$, with $n = [K:\mathbb{Q}]$, $r_1$ real and $r_2$ complex embedding pairs.

title: Class Group Finiteness and Positivity
content: The theorems `classGroup_finite` and `classNumber_pos` are proved by `inferInstance` and direct Mathlib invocation respectively. This is the 'tip of the iceberg' pattern: Mathlib's `instFintypeClassGroup` instance encapsulates hundreds of lines of formalization (the canonical embedding, ideal lattice theory, and the Minkowski bound application) in a single typeclass resolution. The gallery's role is to surface and document these results. The class number $h(K) = |\mathrm{Cl}(K)| \geq 1$ because the trivial class (principal ideals) always exists.

title: Class Number 1 as PID Criterion
content: The equivalence $h(K) = 1 \iff \mathcal{O}_K$ is a PID connects the abstract group-theoretic invariant to a concrete algebraic property. The class group $\mathrm{Cl}(K)$ measures failure of unique factorization: it is trivial precisely when every ideal is principal. For imaginary quadratic fields $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-d})$, Heegner-Stark proved that $h = 1$ only for $d \in \{1,2,3,7,11,19,43,67,163\}$ — making the PID criterion a powerful tool. For practical computation, one checks all prime ideals of norm $\leq M(K)$.
mathContext: $h(K) = 1 \iff \mathcal{O}_K$ is a PID $\iff$ every ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ is principal. Example: $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-5}]$ has $h = 2$ since $(2, 1+\sqrt{-5})$ is not principal.

title: The Minkowski Bound Formula
content: The bound $M(K) = (4/\pi)^{r_2} \cdot (n!/n^n) \cdot \sqrt{|\mathrm{disc}(K)|}$ arises from optimizing the convex body shape: the cross-polytope $\{\sum|x_i| + 2\sum|z_j| \leq t\}$ has volume $2^{r_1}(\pi/2)^{r_2} t^n/n!$. Setting this equal to $2^n$ times the lattice covolume and solving for the norm bound yields $M(K)$. The factor $(4/\pi)^{r_2}$ reflects the complex embeddings ($\mathbb{C} \cong \mathbb{R}^2$ contributes $\pi$ to the unit ball volume), and $n!/n^n \sim \sqrt{2\pi n}/e^n$ by Stirling. For quadratic fields: $M(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d})) = \frac{2}{\pi}\sqrt{|d|}$ (imaginary) or $\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{d}$ (real).

title: The Rational Case: $h(\mathbb{Q}) = 1$ and $\mathbb{Z}$ is a PID
content: For $K = \mathbb{Q}$: $n = 1$, $r_1 = 1$, $r_2 = 0$, $|\mathrm{disc}(\mathbb{Q})| = 1$, so $M(\mathbb{Q}) = (1!/1^1) \cdot 1 = 1$. The only integral ideal of $\mathbb{Z}$ with norm $\leq 1$ is $\mathbb{Z}$ itself (the unit ideal), which is principal. Hence every ideal class is trivial, giving $h(\mathbb{Q}) = 1$. The corollary `rat_integers_isPID` follows by rewriting with the PID criterion. This validates the entire framework on the simplest case.
mathContext: $M(\mathbb{Q}) = 1$. Only ideal with $\mathrm{Nm}(I) \leq 1$ is $\mathbb{Z}$. So $h(\mathbb{Q}) = 1$ and $\mathbb{Z}$ is a PID.

title: Closing: Five Verified Theorems and Mathlib Pointers
content: The closing comment catalogues the five fully verified theorems (0 sorries, 0 axioms) exposed as gallery aliases, and points to the two Mathlib modules that underpin this file. The deep formalization lives in `CanonicalEmbedding.ConvexBody`: the theorem `exists_ne_zero_mem_ideal_of_norm_le` is where Minkowski's convex body theorem is actually applied — it constructs a nonzero element of bounded norm in any ideal class, bridging the geometric argument (volume of $B(t)$ versus lattice covolume of $\sigma(I)$) to the algebraic conclusion (bounded norm ideal in every class $\Rightarrow$ finitely many classes).
mathContext: Five theorems: $|\mathrm{Cl}(\mathcal{O}_K)| < \infty$; $h(K) \geq 1$; $h(K)=1 \iff \mathcal{O}_K$ PID; $h(\mathbb{Q})=1$; $\mathbb{Z}$ PID. All via Mathlib's `NumberField.ClassNumber` and `mixedEmbedding.exists_ne_zero_mem_ideal_of_norm_le`.
